A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LoLCATs. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original linearization experiments on Mistral and Llama models, including benchmark accuracy, perplexity, generation efficiency, ablations, and qualitative outputs.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds smaller-model evaluations, hybrid-model experiments, repeated-run results, retrieval tests, and training-dynamics analyses.

M1.justification: v3 adds a hybrid variant retaining Llama 3 8B's first 16 softmax-attention layers, linearizing the remaining layers, and using attention transfer without subsequent LoRA adjustment (B.2). The default two-stage method, attention formulation, and block-wise transfer remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v3 adds CommonsenseQA examples to linearizing training and introduces synthetic passkey-retrieval training and evaluation (B.5.2). This extends coverage to explicit retrieval across long contexts and passkey positions; the existing Alpaca, RedPajama, and LM Evaluation Harness coverage is retained.

E2.justification: New comparisons include MOHAWK's Phi-Mamba and Hybrid Phi-Mamba, plus pretrained alternatives such as xLSTM, DeltaNet, and GLA (Tables 14–15). v3 also adds full finetuning to the LoRA-rank comparison and instruction-tuned and Alpaca-finetuned Transformer controls for retrieval. The main 7–8B comparator roster is retained.

E3.justification: Added protocols include Llama 3.2 1B and Phi 1.5 1.3B configurations with smaller feature maps, full finetuning at learning rate 1e-5, and LoRA adjustment explicitly optimized for attention MSE. Retrieval uses 8192-token training sequences and exact-match evaluation across 2048–10240 tokens and placement deciles. These extend, rather than replace, the original main protocols.

E4.justification: v3 adds retained-softmax-layer and full-finetuning controls, task-matched training-data experiments, retrieval robustness across lengths and positions, and layer-wise LoRA/MSE analyses (B.2, B.4.1, B.5.2, B.7.1–2). Existing rank, projection, window, token-budget, and block-wise analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v3 B.1.2 newly reports means and standard deviations across seeds 0, 1, and 2 for Hedgehog and LoLCATs on Llama 3 8B. This is a limited extension of uncertainty reporting; v1 provides no corresponding repeated-run count, so an increase from a known earlier count cannot be established.

E6.justification: v3 adds smaller-model, hybrid, full-finetuning, repeated-run, retrieval, and training-dynamics results. Examples include 65.8% hybrid-model MMLU and 8K retrieval accuracy of 0% with Alpaca linearizing data versus 100% with passkey data. Main LoLCATs scores are retained, but Mamba2-Llama 3, 50% Attn. changes from 78.4 to 79.5 on HellaSwag and 69.0 to 71.5 on Winogrande; its six-task average rises from 70.4 to 71.0, exceeding LoLCATs' unchanged 70.7 (v1 Table 4; v3 Table 3).

T1.justification: v3 adds explicit cost reasoning for output matching versus attention-weight matching, contrasting O(n) with O(n^2) memory, and states the M/b serial block-training time multiplier (3.1, 3.3.2). The attention identities, losses, and effective-sequence-length definition are otherwise retained or equivalently condensed; no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: attention transfer followed by low-rank adjustment, efficient high-quality linearization, and scaling to 70B and 405B models. Additional appendix evidence does not redefine these headline claims.

C2.justification: v3 links MMLU difficulties to contextual retrieval and identifies a concrete applicability limitation: Alpaca-based linearization can destroy passkey retrieval, while task-matched data restores it (B.5.2). It also adds hypotheses about LoRA limiting harmful updates and interprets projection-specific training dynamics. v1 left long-context capability largely to future work.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly documents learning-rate searches and parameter-selection decisions. Appendix C.1 substantially expands pseudocode for sliding-window hybrids, block-wise losses, and LoRA adjustment; B.5.2 supplies training-data construction and the retrieval prompt template. These are documentation additions, not evidence that retained experiments changed settings.

R1.justification: v3 adds references supporting MOHAWK comparisons, smaller models, CommonsenseQA, and retrieval/context studies, and sharpens the memory comparison with Hedgehog. The extended related-work discussion and overall positioning as efficient Transformer linearization remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites clarify attention transfer and block-wise execution, label method sections as Parts 1 and 2, and reorganize Appendix B. The block-wise quality discussion moves into B.7.3. Most existing prose remains; v3 also introduces an unresolved equation reference in the introduction.

P2.justification: v3 adds two main-text algorithm boxes, eight result tables, retrieval heatmaps, and several LoRA-dynamics figures, alongside expanded code listings. It relocates the block-wise comparison from v1 Table 3 to v3 Table 24. Existing plot images and Appendix E artifacts are retained.

improvement.justification: The repeated-run results and full-finetuning control substantially strengthen the empirical support, while retrieval experiments replace v1's untested long-context boundary with a documented failure and task-dependent recovery. Expanded implementation guidance improves transparency. These gains outweigh reporting shortcomings, including B.6's retained claim of outperforming the hybrid baseline despite the updated Table 3 scores no longer supporting that comparison.
